hint.socks5_port_4145: hint: {n:,} proxies ({pct:.1f}%) in input are on port 4145, the conventional SOCKS4 daemon port. They are likely SOCKS4, mislabeled as socks5. With -p socks5 you'll see tunnel/MITM pass but 'err' (ConnectionReset/ServerDisconnected) during HTTPS payload transfer. Try the same list with `-p socks4`; expect more 'good' results.
input.no_input: no proxy input. Pipe a list via stdin (e.g. `proxine http -s | proxyprof -p http`) or use `-f FILE`.
input.no_valid_pairs: no valid IP:PORT pairs in input.

input.judge_must_be_http: --judge must start with http:// or https://
judge.cf_warn_intro: This affects your scan results in 3 important ways:
judge.cf_warn_effect1:
1) CF bot management may block some proxies (especially datacenter ASNs and IPs
       listed in public proxy databases) with 403/503 BEFORE they reach the judge.
       Those proxies will appear as 'fail' even though they are technically alive.
       Results skew toward 'CF-friendly' residential / clean IPs.
judge.cf_warn_effect2:
2) The judge is HTTPS; HTTP-forwarding-only proxies (old squids that can't CONNECT)
       cannot reach it at all → 'fail'. You will not detect that class of proxy.
judge.cf_warn_effect3:
3) UPSIDE: the CF-IPCountry header gives you free per-proxy country info
       (COUNTRY column) — no extra GeoIP DB or API calls needed.
judge.cf_warn_alt_custom: A) -j https://your-judge.tld/azenv.php → use your own non-CF judge URL (self-hosted azenv-compatible script, or another public non-CF judge).
judge.cf_warn_alt_skip: B) --no-judge → skip the judge probe entirely. Anonymity classification (L1/L2/L2d/L3) is NOT performed; only connectivity + tunnel + access tests remain. RELIABILITY DROPS — a proxy you thought was anonymous may actually be transparent. Use only when you care about reachability/HTTPS-capability, not anonymity.
judge.cf_aborted: user aborted scan with CF judge.
judge.all_defaults_cf: warning: all default judges appear to be behind CF; expect biased results (use -j for a custom non-CF judge).
judge.unavail_intro: No working judge was found. You can try one of the following:
judge.unavail_hint_net: 1) Check your internet connection (e.g. `ping httpheader.net` or `curl -I http://httpheader.net/azenv.php`). Server firewall may be blocking outbound 80/443.
judge.unavail_hint_timeout: 2) Increase the timeout: `-T 10` (default 3s; judges may not respond fast enough on slow links).
judge.unavail_hint_custom: 3) Specify your own judge URL: `-j https://your-host.tld/azenv.php` (use the bundled proxyjudge.php on any PHP host).
judge.unavail_hint_skip: 4) Skip judge entirely: `--no-judge`. No anonymity classification (L1/L2/L2d/L3) and no country info; only connectivity/tunnel/access tests run. Fastest fix if you only care about reachability.
cli.description: Profile a list of proxies: connectivity, anonymity level (elite / anonymous / transparent), and optional access test. Designed to chain after `proxine`.
cli.example.pipe: Pipe proxine output, keep only elite (with CONNECT tunnel test)
cli.example.file_in: File in, elite+anon, save to file
cli.example.access_test: Add 3 random CF gatekeepers to the filter
cli.example.no_tunnel: Skip CONNECT test (faster, accepts non-tunnel proxies)
cli.example.cf_judge: Use your CF-protected judge (adds country info + visit logs)
cli.group.scan_desc: Scan behaviour — concurrency, timeouts, probes. These drive network cost.
cli.group.filter_desc: Post-scan filters — gate the output list. No extra network cost.
cli.group.output_desc: Where the output goes and how loud stderr is.
cli.help.protocol: Proxy protocol of all entries in the list.
cli.help.keep_local_ips: Do NOT filter local-network IPs (RFC1918, loopback, link-local, multicast) from the input. Default: local addresses are dropped — seeing 192.168.x.y in a public proxy list is usually a copy-paste mistake.
cli.help.judge: Custom judge URL. Identity header sent only to trusted domains: {domains}.
cli.help.no_judge: Skip the judge probe entirely. No anonymity classification (L1/L2/L2d/L3), no outbound IP, no country info — only connectivity + tunnel + access tests run. Faster scan, but RELIABILITY DROPS — a proxy reported as 'ok' may actually be transparent and leak your IP.
cli.help.user_agent: User-Agent header sent in all probes (default: Firefox 125). Override when judge/gatekeeper has bot detection that rejects the default UA.
cli.help.access_test: Gatekeeper filter. Value 'cloudflare' (or no value/default) = {count} random CF-protected sites (Cloudflare WAF/Bot test). 'google' = {count} random Google domains (generate_204 reachability test). Otherwise = comma-separated URLs. Default: off. Note: CF/Google presets are HTTPS; HTTP-only proxies that can't tunnel will fail this filter — pair with --no-tunnel-test --no-access-test for HTTP forwarding-only scans.
cli.help.no_access_test: Skip access-test entirely. Recommended for HTTP-only forwarding proxies (target sites use plain HTTP only).
cli.help.access_strict: Switch access-test to strict mode: ALL gatekeeper URLs must pass (legacy behavior). Default is any-of — proxy passes if at least 1 URL succeeds. Strict mode inflates cumulative fail rate (0.8³≈51%%) but enforces tighter filtering.
cli.help.access_timeout: Per-access-probe timeout in seconds. Default: --timeout × 2 (HTTPS+CONNECT+TLS needs more RTT than HTTP-only judge). Probes run in PARALLEL; this timeout applies per URL, not cumulative.
cli.help.tunnel_test: HTTPS CONNECT probe (default: on). Probe URL: {url}. Note: for HTTP forwarding-only proxies (plain HTTP target sites, no HTTPS), use --no-tunnel-test to keep them in output.
cli.help.mitm_test: Drop TLS-intercepting (MITM) proxies from output (default: on). Needs --tunnel-test.
cli.help.reputation: SQLite reputation DB. HOT/WARM/NEW/COLD buckets + exponential probation. Default: {default}
cli.help.cold_timeout: Short timeout for COLD bucket probes, seconds (default: {default}).
cli.help.level: Max anonymity level (filter): 1=elite only, 2=elite+anon, 3=all (default: {default} → no filter, all working proxies reported in the table).
cli.help.country: Keep only these ISO country codes (e.g. TR,US,DE). Needs CF-aware judge. Mutually exclusive with --exclude-country.
cli.help.exclude_country: Drop proxies from these ISO country codes (e.g. CN,RU). Mutually exclusive with --country.
cli.help.exclude_distorting: Drop distorting proxies (those that inject a fake IP). Auto-enabled for socks4 — SOCKS4 by spec doesn't touch headers, so any L2d is a sign of mislabeling/chain; disable with --no-exclude-distorting.
cli.help.allow_tunnel_fail: Include proxies that failed the CONNECT tunnel test (test still runs, result shown in table).
cli.help.allow_mitm: Include MITM-suspected proxies — risky for HTTPS security.
cli.help.allow_access_fail: Include proxies that failed the access test (couldn't reach gatekeepers).
cli.help.output: Write filtered list to FILE (default: stdout).
cli.help.retest_output: If -o file exists and is non-empty, add its contents to the input list (re-test the previous scan's working proxies in this run). Default: on. Use --no-retest-output to scan only the new input.
cli.help.top_n: Scan only the N most likely-good proxies from input: ordered HOT (most recent success first) → WARM → NEW, COLD bucket skipped entirely. Requires reputation DB. Useful for fast health checks (e.g. lighter scan every 15min).
cli.help.export_good: Don't scan; dump HOT+WARM proxies from the reputation DB to stdout (recency-sorted). -p/--protocol required. Example: `proxyprof -p socks5 --export-good > working.lst`.
cli.help.silent: Write list to stdout only; suppress stderr.
cli.help.lang: UI language: {supported} (default: system locale → {default}). Env: PROXYPROF_LANG.
cli.help.db_stats: Summarize the reputation DB and exit (no scan). -p/--protocol not required.
cli.help.verify_gatekeepers: Probe default CF gatekeeper URLs directly (no proxy); write alive ones to ~/.config/proxyprof/gatekeepers.txt overlay. Subsequent scans read this overlay. -p not required.
cli.help.debug: Write every access/tunnel probe to FILE as JSONL (default: debug.log). Includes UA, status, CF headers, body snippet, exception details.
progress.format: [{bar}] {pct:3.0f}%  {done:>{digits}}/{total}  ok:{ok:<4}  dropped:{drop:<4}  fail:{fail:<4}  skip:{skip:<4}  rate:{rate:5.1f}/s  cpu:{cpu:5.1f}%  mem:{mem:4.0f}MB  net:{net}  elapsed:{elapsed:5.1f}s
progress.legend:
LEVEL
    L1   Elite         your IP and proxy presence are fully hidden; the strongest anonymity.
    L2   Anonymous     IP is hidden but Via/X-Forwarded-* headers reveal a proxy is in use.
    L2d  Distorting    L2 plus injects a FAKE public IP into X-Forwarded-For (fingerprint trick).
    L3   Transparent   your real IP appears in headers; no anonymity, just routing.

  COLUMNS (✓ = desirable outcome)
    TUNNEL      proxy supports HTTPS via CONNECT (HTTP-only proxies can't reach most modern sites).
    NO MITM     proxy isn't tampering with TLS, no man-in-the-middle. HTTPS is safe.
progress.hint_press_d_show: Press 'd' to show details (level codes + column meanings).
progress.hint_press_dpq: Press 'd' for details, 'p' to pause/resume, 'q' for controlled exit.
progress.paused: ⏸  Paused — no new tasks dispatched; in-flight ones will finish. Press 'p' again to resume.
progress.quit_requested: ⚠  Graceful shutdown — pending tasks skipped, in-flight will finish. Press 'q' again for IMMEDIATE exit.
progress.legend_access_cloudflare:
ACCESS      Cloudflare WAF/Bot test: reach {n} random CF-protected sites
                (cloudflare/discord/reddit/medium/...) at the /cdn-cgi/trace endpoint.
                Otherwise a 3-char code:
                  Nxx  = HTTP non-2xx (e.g. 403 block/CF-bot, 503 challenge, 429 rate-limit, 404 not-found)
                  to   = request timed out
                  err  = network error (refused / disconnected / payload / reset)
                  mitm = TLS chain broken (cert verify failed) → proxy is intercepting, HTTPS NOT safe
                  ?    = unexpected exception
progress.legend_access_google:
ACCESS      Google reachability test: reach {n} random Google domains
                (google/gstatic/youtube/accounts/...) at the /generate_204 endpoint.
                Otherwise a 3-char code:
                  Nxx  = HTTP non-2xx (e.g. 403 block/CF-bot, 503 challenge, 429 rate-limit, 404 not-found)
                  to   = request timed out
                  err  = network error (refused / disconnected / payload / reset)
                  mitm = TLS chain broken (cert verify failed) → proxy is intercepting, HTTPS NOT safe
                  ?    = unexpected exception
progress.legend_access_custom:
ACCESS      Custom test ({n} URLs): reach ALL user-provided URLs.
                Otherwise a 3-char code:
                  Nxx  = HTTP non-2xx (e.g. 403 block/CF-bot, 503 challenge, 429 rate-limit, 404 not-found)
                  to   = request timed out
                  err  = network error (refused / disconnected / payload / reset)
                  mitm = TLS chain broken (cert verify failed) → proxy is intercepting, HTTPS NOT safe
                  ?    = unexpected exception
value.judge_incomplete_count: {n} (judge response missing REMOTE_ADDR — likely CF challenge / DNS hijack / truncated body; L1 result is unreliable)
warn.http_proxy_https_judge: warning: HTTP proxy + HTTPS judge. Anonymity detection depends on TLS-tunnel behaviour; CONNECT-incapable proxies fall through to HTTP forwarding and may appear as L2/L2d, while CONNECT-capable proxies will mostly look L1. For more reliable anonymity classification, drop -j to use the built-in HTTP judges.

misc.verify_intro: probing {n} default CF gatekeeper URLs (no proxy, direct)...
misc.verify_no_alive: no gatekeeper alive — overlay not written; check your network connection.
misc.verify_written: overlay written: {path} (subsequent scans will use this list)
misc.debug_enabled: debug logging on → {path} (every access/tunnel probe written as JSONL)
misc.unsupported_lang: unsupported language '{lang}'. Available: {supported}. Falling back to '{fallback}'.
misc.export_good_needs_protocol: --export-good requires -p/--protocol (each protocol has its own DB).
misc.top_n_needs_reputation: --top-n requires a reputation DB; cannot be used with --no-reputation.
misc.force_quit_finished: force exit complete — proxies found so far have been written to -o; RESULT box and reputation update skipped.
